risk: Facilities are drawn on incomplete or unenforceable documentation, so the bank cannot enforce its rights on default.
audit_objective: Confirm credit documentation is complete, executed and enforceable before drawdown.
what_to_review: Completeness of the credit file — agreements, security, conditions precedent
Execution and legal review of non-standard documentation
Conditions precedent satisfied before disbursement
Document custody and retrieval
Covenant terms recorded in the monitoring system
procedures: Sample facilities and test the credit file for executed agreements and evidence of conditions precedent.
Test that non-standard terms received legal review before execution.
Test whether covenants in the agreement were loaded into the monitoring system, and completely.
Test document custody by requesting original security documents for a sample.
red_flags: Drawdowns before conditions precedent satisfied
Covenants in the agreement absent from monitoring
Original documents that cannot be located
Non-standard terms agreed without legal review

risk: Security is unperfected or valued on stale information, so realisable value on default is far below what is recorded.
audit_objective: Confirm collateral is legally perfected and valued on a current, independent basis.
what_to_review: Legal perfection — registration, charges, priority
Valuation frequency by asset class and independence of valuers
Loan-to-value monitoring and breach action
Insurance over charged assets
Release of security and its authorisation
procedures: Test perfection evidence for a sample of secured exposures, including registration at the relevant registry.
Test valuation currency against policy and re-perform loan-to-value calculations.
Test valuer independence and panel rotation.
Test that insurance over charged assets is current and the bank is noted as interested party.
red_flags: Charges unregistered or registered late
Valuations years out of date on volatile asset classes
Same valuer used for all exposures to one borrower
Insurance lapsed on charged property

risk: Borrower covenant breaches are not detected, so deterioration is not acted on and the bank loses its intervention rights.
audit_objective: Confirm borrower covenants are monitored and breaches escalated and acted upon.
what_to_review: Completeness of covenants captured from agreements
Receipt and review of borrower financial information
Timeliness of covenant testing after each reporting date
Waiver and amendment authority
Link between breach and risk grading or staging
procedures: Recompute covenants for a sample of borrowers from their submitted financials.
Test whether borrower information was received on time and chased when late.
Test waivers granted for authorisation at the correct level and for whether pricing or security was adjusted.
Test whether breaches fed through to risk grading.
red_flags: Waivers granted routinely to the same borrowers
Financial information outstanding for months
Covenants recomputed only at year end
Breaches with no effect on grading

risk: Deteriorating exposures are not moved to specialist management early enough, reducing recovery.
audit_objective: Assess whether early warning indicators work and problem exposures are managed by the right people.
what_to_review: Early warning indicator design, coverage and response
Watchlist criteria and transfer to specialist workout
Independence of workout from origination
Recovery strategies and their execution
Provisioning alignment with the workout view
procedures: Test whether early warning indicators triggered and what happened when they did.
Compare the date deterioration was observable in data to the date the exposure was watchlisted.
Test that workout management is independent of the originating relationship manager.
Compare recovery outcomes to strategies agreed at transfer.
red_flags: Exposures watchlisted only once past due
Relationship managers retaining problem exposures
Indicators triggering with no recorded response
Recovery strategies never revisited

subprocess: Credit Risk Models and Rating Integrity
risk: Internal ratings and credit models are inaccurate or overridden, understating risk and regulatory capital.
audit_objective: Assess the integrity, validation and use of internal credit ratings and models.
what_to_review: Model development, validation and approval governance
Rating override frequency, direction and justification
Data quality feeding models
Back-testing of predicted against actual default
Use test — whether ratings actually drive decisions and pricing
procedures: Analyse rating overrides by direction and originator; overrides consistently improving ratings warrant testing.
Review validation reports and test whether findings were remediated.
Back-test rating performance against realised defaults.
Test whether ratings genuinely drive pricing and approval, or are produced after the decision.
red_flags: Overrides almost always upward
Validation findings open across cycles
Models unchanged despite deteriorating performance
Ratings assigned after the credit decision

risk: Exposure concentrations breach regulatory or internal limits because connected counterparties are not grouped correctly.
audit_objective: Confirm exposures are aggregated correctly and remain within limits.
what_to_review: Connected counterparty identification and grouping
Aggregation across products, entities and geographies
Regulatory large exposure limits and internal appetite
Sector, geographic and collateral concentration
Breach identification and escalation
procedures: Test the grouping of connected counterparties against ownership and control data.
Recompute large exposures against regulatory limits at several dates.
Analyse concentration by sector and geography against appetite.
Test escalation of breaches and whether limits were raised rather than exposures reduced.
red_flags: Connected borrowers treated as unrelated
Exposure aggregation excluding off-balance sheet commitments
Limits raised immediately after a breach
Concentration reported only at year end
evidence: Exposure data by counterparty and group

subprocess: Customer Due Diligence and Risk Rating
risk: Customer risk is rated incorrectly at onboarding, so the level of due diligence and monitoring applied is wrong from the start.
audit_objective: Confirm customer risk rating drives due diligence and is refreshed as behaviour changes.
what_to_review: Risk rating methodology and its factors
Enhanced due diligence for high-risk customers and PEPs
Beneficial ownership identification and verification
Periodic review cycles by risk tier
Rating overrides and who may make them
procedures: Sample customers across risk tiers and test that due diligence matches the rating applied.
Test beneficial ownership identification for corporate customers, including layered structures.
Test rating overrides for approval and rationale.
Quantify overdue periodic reviews and test whether high-risk customers continued transacting.
red_flags: Ratings downgraded to avoid enhanced due diligence
Beneficial ownership recorded as the immediate holder only
Periodic reviews overdue on the highest-risk customers
Overrides made by relationship staff

risk: Correspondent and trade finance relationships are used to move illicit funds because the underlying activity is not scrutinised.
audit_objective: Assess controls over higher-risk financial crime channels.
what_to_review: Correspondent bank due diligence and Wolfsberg-style questionnaires
Nested and downstream relationship identification
Trade document review for dual-use goods and price manipulation
Sanctions screening on trade parties, vessels and ports
Country and product risk assessment
procedures: Test correspondent due diligence currency and whether nested relationships were identified.
Sample trade transactions and test document review for over- or under-invoicing and dual-use goods.
Test vessel and port screening on shipping documents.
Test whether high-risk corridors receive additional scrutiny.
red_flags: Correspondent questionnaires years old
Nested relationships discovered by the regulator
Trade documents reviewed for form only
Vessels not screened

risk: Customers are defrauded through account takeover, authorised push payment scams or card fraud, and the bank bears loss and censure.
audit_objective: Assess the effectiveness of fraud prevention, detection and customer reimbursement.
what_to_review: Authentication and step-up controls for payments and account changes
Fraud detection rules, machine learning models and their tuning
Confirmation of payee and scam warnings
Reimbursement decisions and their consistency
Mule account detection
procedures: Analyse fraud losses by type and channel and test whether controls were adjusted after each pattern emerged.
Test authentication for high-risk actions such as payee changes and device registration.
Review reimbursement decisions for consistency with the regulatory standard.
Test mule account detection — accounts receiving and rapidly dispersing funds.
red_flags: Losses rising in a channel with no rule change
Reimbursement declined inconsistently
Mule accounts identified only after victim reports
Step-up authentication bypassable through a channel

subprocess: Anti-Bribery, Corruption and Tax Evasion Facilitation
risk: The bank facilitates bribery or tax evasion through its customers or its own conduct, triggering corporate criminal liability.
audit_objective: Assess the adequacy of procedures to prevent facilitation of financial crime by staff and associates.
what_to_review: Risk assessment for bribery and facilitation of tax evasion
Gifts, hospitality and political donation controls
Third-party intermediaries and introducer arrangements
Training for high-risk roles
Investigation and reporting of suspected facilitation
procedures: Test the bribery and facilitation risk assessment for coverage of the actual business model.
Review the gifts and hospitality register for completeness and approval of high-value items.
Test due diligence on introducers and intermediaries and the basis of their remuneration.
Test training completion for high-risk and client-facing roles.
red_flags: Introducers paid success fees with no due diligence
Gifts register with implausibly few entries
Risk assessment not covering key jurisdictions
Training completion low in front-office roles

risk: Cash and negotiable instruments are misappropriated at branches through teller manipulation or vault control failure.
audit_objective: Assess physical and procedural controls over cash and instruments in branch operations.
what_to_review: Teller limits, cash-outs and end-of-day balancing
Vault dual control and access logging
Surprise cash counts and their independence
Suspense and difference accounts at branch level
Negotiable instrument stock control
procedures: Perform surprise cash counts at a sample of branches and agree to records.
Analyse teller differences by individual — small persistent differences can indicate skimming.
Test vault access logs for single-person access events.
Review branch suspense accounts for aged items.
red_flags: Recurring small teller differences by the same person
Vault accessed by one person
Surprise counts announced in advance
Suspense items cleared just before a count
evidence: Cash records and teller balancing reports

risk: Payments fail, settle late or are duplicated, causing customer loss, liquidity impact and regulatory breach.
audit_objective: Assess controls over payment processing, settlement and exception handling.
what_to_review: Straight-through processing rates and manual repair volumes
Cut-off times, settlement finality and liquidity management
Duplicate and erroneous payment detection and recovery
Payment scheme rules compliance
Resilience of payment channels and contingency arrangements
procedures: Analyse manual repair volumes and who performs them; manual intervention is where error and fraud enter.
Test duplicate payment detection and the recovery of identified duplicates.
Test compliance with scheme rules on timing and messaging standards.
Review payment incidents and test whether root causes were remediated.
red_flags: High manual repair rates in one channel
Repairs performed by the same person who inputs
Duplicates identified by customers rather than the bank
Recurring incidents with the same cause

risk: Complaints are not identified, investigated fairly or used to detect systemic customer harm.
audit_objective: Assess whether complaint handling is fair, timely and drives correction of root causes.
what_to_review: Complaint identification — including expressions of dissatisfaction not logged as complaints
Investigation quality, timeliness and outcome fairness
Root cause analysis and systemic issue identification
Redress calculation and delivery
Ombudsman referrals and overturn rates
procedures: Sample closed complaints and reassess whether the outcome was fair on the facts.
Test whether complaints are being logged at first point of contact or filtered out.
Test whether root causes were identified and remediated, including proactive redress for similarly affected customers.
Analyse ombudsman overturn rates as an indicator of internal decision quality.
red_flags: Complaints resolved verbally and never logged
High ombudsman overturn rate
Redress paid only to those who complained
Root cause recorded as "customer misunderstanding"

risk: Products are sold to customers for whom they are unsuitable, or perform differently from what was represented.
audit_objective: Assess whether products are designed, targeted and monitored for good customer outcomes.
what_to_review: Product approval process and target market definition
Distribution against the intended target market
Fair value assessment and pricing
Post-sale monitoring of customer outcomes
Vulnerable customer identification and treatment
procedures: Test sales data against the defined target market and quantify sales outside it.
Review the fair value assessment for products with high margin or low usage.
Test outcome monitoring — cancellation rates, complaints, claims declined — for signals of poor outcomes.
Test identification and treatment of vulnerable customers in the sales process.
red_flags: Products sold well outside the target market
Fair value assessments concluding value in every case
High early cancellation rates unexplained
Vulnerability flags not visible to front-line staff
